glossary.means: the corporate regulator. It licenses financial advice businesses, sets the guidance they work to, and bans people from the industry.
glossary.matters: an ASIC action is usually the item that changes what an adviser does, which is why these land as ACT.
glossary.check: asic.gov.au

glossary.means: the prudential regulator. It supervises banks, insurers and super funds for financial soundness, where ASIC watches conduct.
glossary.matters: an APRA item is usually about an institution's stability rather than about advice practice.
glossary.check: apra.gov.au

glossary.means: the free external complaints scheme. A consumer who cannot resolve a complaint with a firm can take it to AFCA, whose determination binds the firm.
glossary.matters: determinations show how obligations are read in a real dispute, which is why they sit in the ACT tier.
glossary.check: afca.org.au

glossary.means: the tribunal that reviews government decisions, including ASIC bannings. It replaced the Administrative Appeals Tribunal in October 2024.
glossary.matters: a ban can be affirmed, varied or set aside here, so an ASIC decision is not always the last word.
glossary.check: art.gov.au

glossary.means: the tax administrator, and the regulator of self-managed super funds.
glossary.matters: it is the primary source for how a tax or SMSF rule is actually applied, ahead of any commentary about it.
glossary.check: ato.gov.au

glossary.means: the main professional association for advisers, formed in 2023 from the merger of the FPA and the AFA.
glossary.matters: it speaks for the profession in consultations. That is a position, not a rule — useful context, rarely an obligation.
glossary.check: faaa.au

glossary.means: a scheme that pays limited compensation to a consumer who has won an AFCA determination the firm has not paid.
glossary.matters: it is funded by a levy on licensees, so changes to how it works change what advice businesses pay.
glossary.check: cslr.org.au, and Treasury for any change to the levy

glossary.means: the licence a business must hold to provide financial services. An adviser either holds one or is authorised under someone else's.
glossary.matters: the licensee carries the obligations, so who holds the licence decides who is answerable.
glossary.check: asic.gov.au

glossary.means: a person or business authorised to provide financial services under another entity's licence.
glossary.matters: it explains why a story about one adviser is often a story about their licensee.
glossary.check: asic.gov.au, and ASIC Connect's professional registers

glossary.means: an ASIC order stopping a person from providing financial services, or controlling a financial services business, for a set period or permanently.
glossary.matters: the reasons given are the closest thing to a worked example of how conduct obligations are applied.
glossary.check: the media release and the banning notice at asic.gov.au

glossary.means: the legal duty to act in the client's best interests when giving personal advice, in the Corporations Act.
glossary.matters: most advice enforcement comes back to it, so it is worth knowing in its own words rather than in summary.
glossary.check: the Corporations Act on legislation.gov.au, and ASIC's guidance

glossary.means: the ethical standards binding financial advisers, covering competence, honesty, fairness and conflicts of interest.
glossary.matters: it sits alongside the law rather than inside it: conduct can meet the Act and still breach the Code.
glossary.check: legislation.gov.au for the instrument, asic.gov.au for how breaches are handled

glossary.means: the government's package of advice reforms, following the Quality of Advice Review — simplifying advice documents and obligations, and proposing a new class of adviser.
glossary.matters: it is the source of most reform talk in the trade press. Much of it is proposed, not law.
glossary.check: treasury.gov.au — and confirm whether a measure is announced, in draft, or in force

glossary.means: the document that sets out personal advice, the reasons for it, and what it costs.
glossary.matters: changes to it are a live reform topic, so check whether a description is current or proposed.
glossary.check: treasury.gov.au for reform status, asic.gov.au for what is required today

glossary.means: the prohibition on offering a financial product to a consumer during, or because of, unsolicited contact.
glossary.matters: it decides how a firm may approach someone who did not ask, including through referrals.
glossary.check: the Corporations Act and ASIC's regulatory guidance

glossary.means: a payment that could reasonably influence advice given to a client. Most forms of it are banned.
glossary.matters: it is the rule behind most stories about commissions and adviser payments.
glossary.check: the Corporations Act and ASIC's guidance

glossary.means: the obligation on a licensee to report certain breaches, and likely breaches, to ASIC within set timeframes.
glossary.matters: the reporting numbers ASIC publishes are where a lot of enforcement attention starts.
glossary.check: asic.gov.au regulatory guidance

glossary.means: the duty on product issuers and distributors to design a product for a defined group of consumers and distribute it to that group.
glossary.matters: it is the obligation behind the target market determination attached to a product.
glossary.check: asic.gov.au regulatory guidance

glossary.means: the document saying which consumers a financial product is designed for, and how it may be distributed.
glossary.matters: distributing outside it is the breach ASIC acts on, so the document is the test.
glossary.check: the product issuer's own TMD, and asic.gov.au

glossary.means: the disclosure document for a financial product — what it is, its risks, and its costs.
glossary.matters: it is the primary source for what a product actually does, ahead of any description of it.
glossary.check: the issuer's current PDS

glossary.means: a superannuation fund run by its own members, who are also its trustees and carry the legal responsibility.
glossary.matters: the trustee obligations, and the ATO's role as regulator, are what separate these from other funds.
glossary.check: ato.gov.au

glossary.means: a proposed additional tax on earnings attributable to very large superannuation balances.
glossary.matters: its thresholds, start date and mechanics have changed more than once. Nothing about it should be taken from a summary.
glossary.check: treasury.gov.au and ato.gov.au for the current status — confirm before relying on any figure

glossary.means: the obligation on super fund trustees to have a strategy for helping members in retirement, not just while they are saving.
glossary.matters: it is why funds have moved into retirement guidance, which touches what advisers do.
glossary.check: apra.gov.au and asic.gov.au

glossary.means: the supervised year a new adviser completes before advising independently, with structured training and a supervisor.
glossary.matters: for someone entering the industry this is the path itself, not background.
glossary.check: asic.gov.au and the FAAA's guidance for new entrants

glossary.means: the ongoing training an adviser must complete each year to stay authorised.
glossary.matters: the requirement is set by law and topped up by the licensee, so counts and categories vary.
glossary.check: asic.gov.au, then your licensee's own policy

glossary.means: a firm's own complaints process, which a consumer uses before AFCA.
glossary.matters: the timeframes and record-keeping are prescribed, and failures here show up in AFCA determinations.
glossary.check: asic.gov.au regulatory guidance

glossary.means: insurance cover that pays where a person is permanently unable to work, usually to a definition set in the policy.
glossary.matters: the definition in the policy decides the claim, and definitions differ between products.
glossary.check: the policy document, and the Life Insurance Code of Practice

glossary.means: the life insurance industry's own code, with a committee that monitors it and can sanction a breaching insurer.
glossary.matters: a code sanction is industry self-regulation, not a regulator's action. Both matter; they are not the same thing.
glossary.check: the code at fsc.org.au, and asic.gov.au for anything regulatory

glossary.means: a client who meets asset or income tests and so receives fewer protections than a retail client.
glossary.matters: the tests, and whether they should change, are a live policy argument. Which category a client is in changes the obligations owed.
glossary.check: the Corporations Act, and treasury.gov.au for any review

glossary.means: an arrangement where a client's portfolio is managed to a model, with the client holding the underlying assets.
glossary.matters: it changes how advice is implemented and reviewed, which is why platform stories dwell on it.
glossary.check: the offer document, and asic.gov.au on the licensing of the service

glossary.means: the total value of money a manager or platform looks after.
glossary.matters: it is a size and momentum figure, not a quality one. Useful as market context, rarely more.
glossary.check: the manager's own reporting

glossary.means: the tax on a gain made when an asset is sold or otherwise disposed of.
glossary.matters: concessions and exemptions do a lot of work here, and they are specific. Never take one from a summary.
glossary.check: ato.gov.au

items.title: TPB provides guidance on reforms to sanctions powers
items.teaser: TPB provides guidance on reforms to sanctions powers tdenp Thu, 2026-09-17 11:59 Media releases The Treasury Laws Amendment (Strengthening Accountability for Tax Adviser Misconduct and Other Measures) Bill 2026 has received Royal Assent, providing for an enhanced sanctions framework for the Tax Practitioners Board…
items.ai_summary: • **TPB has published guidance on new sanctions powers** following the Royal Assent of the Treasury Laws Amendment Bill 2026. • Advisers must understand the enhanced sanctions framework to avoid penalties for misconduct or non-compliance.

items.title: ASIC halts Remara's private credit products for TMD deficiencies
items.teaser: ASIC has slapped interim stop orders on Remara Investment Management's private credit products over deficiencies in its target market determination (TMD), claiming they were too risky for retail investors.
items.ai_summary: • **ASIC has halted Remara's private credit products** due to TMD deficiencies, affecting retail investors. • Advisers must avoid recommending these products and ensure compliance with ASIC's interim stop orders.

items.title: FAAA calls for review of proposed data breach report deadline
items.teaser: The Financial Advice Association Australia’s submission to privacy reform consultation recommends clarifications including how certain points will work alongside existing regulations, and a review of the 72-hour data breach report deadline.
items.ai_summary: • **FAAA calls for review of the 72-hour data breach report deadline** for small businesses. • Advisers should be aware of the challenges in meeting the deadline and the need for clarity on when the period starts.

items.title: ASIC makes interim stop orders on three private credit products
items.teaser: ASIC has issued interim stop orders against three private credit products run by MSC over deficiencies with their target market determinations (TMDs). The three MSC products are the 6 Month (Fixed and Variable) Account, 12 Month (Fixed and Variable) Account and At Call Account.

items.title: Consultation on the application of the waterfall framework for the 2026–27 CSLR special levy
items.teaser: In the paper, the Government has outlined three tiers for proposed special levy allocation with Tier 1 allocated $10 million, in addition to the $20 million annual levy and covering financial advice, Tier 2 to contribute $40 million from responsible entities of managed investment schemes (MISs) and Tier 3 $120.262…

items.title: Treasury opens consultation for CSLR special levy
items.teaser: On 21 September, Treasury launched consultation on its proposed waterfall framework to fund the 2026-27 special levy after the financial advice sub-sector cap was exceeded by $170.3 million in the most recent revised estimates.
items.ai_summary: • **Treasury launched consultation on a waterfall framework** to fund the 2026-27 CSLR special levy after exceeding the financial advice sub-sector cap by **$170.3 million**. • Advisers must prepare for potential cost allocations under the new framework, which aims to distribute levy costs across financial services sub-sectors to ensure sustainability.

items.title: Div 296 spares those who die in FY27, but estates inherit future bills
items.teaser: With Division 296 now in its first year of operation, advisers with clients holding large super balances are facing a new layer of estate planning considerations, particularly when it comes to how the tax applies once a client dies.

items.title: Consultation opens on data gaps in managed investment schemes
items.teaser: Treasury has released a consultation paper providing new details on the regulation of managed investment schemes (MIS). There is around $3 trillion dollars invested in registered and unregistered MISs in Australia and the paper is seeking feedback on proposals to address data gaps.

items.title: Class action against Macquarie echoes soon-to-be-eliminated ‘but for’ determinations
items.teaser: A class action against Macquarie Investment Management over its role in the collapse of the Shield master fund claims it should compensate investors for investment returns they missed out on by not being invested somewhere else.
items.ai_summary: • **A class action against Macquarie** mirrors the soon-to-be-eliminated “but for” determinations under AFCA. • The case highlights investor claims for lost growth and distress, which may not be resolved under the new framework, prompting legal and advisory considerations for affected clients.

items.title: Claude for advisers has regulators and competitors on alert
items.teaser: ASIC says it is closely monitoring developments such as the new Claude for financial advisers’ plugin – launched this week – and its potential implications for the Australian market. Incumbent tech vendors are also watching.
items.ai_summary: • **ASIC is monitoring Claude’s potential impact** on the financial advice industry as it may affect regulatory requirements and market dynamics. • Advisers should stay informed about AI developments and consider how they might integrate such tools in the future.

items.title: Div 296 no hurdle to SMSF establishments, Class research finds
items.teaser: There’s never been more money in self-managed super funds than there is today, and the rate they’re being created has never been faster.
items.ai_summary: • **Over 52,000 new SMSFs were established in FY26**, the highest ever, with total funds surpassing 680,000. • **Div 296 hasn’t deterred SMSF growth**, showing strong consumer interest despite regulatory challenges.

items.title: ‘Well beyond warnings’: ASIC tightens the screws on private credit funds
items.teaser: Private credit managers are “well beyond warnings”, according to ASIC, as it urges them to improve practices by the end of the year.

items.title: Paraplanning’s Next Era: Strategic, Tech-Driven, Compliance-Led
items.teaser: Silvia Wade Founder of Mutual Paraplanning Services Paraplanning’s Next Era: Strategic, Tech Driven, Compliance Led For a long time, people in our profession have viewed paraplanners as note-takers and creators…
items.ai_summary: • Modern paraplanners are now strategic partners and compliance gatekeepers, not just note-takers

items.title: Court ruling highlights member benefits and disputes in intergenerational wealth transfer
items.teaser: In Topp, in the matter of McLennan Holdings Pty Limited (In Liq) [2026] FCA 1259, Justice Yaseen Shariff backed a court-appointed receiver’s decision not to pursue legal action against family members or a financial adviser over transactions that shifted millions of dollars from the retirement benefits of elderly fund…
items.ai_summary: • Court ruled against pursuing legal action over intergenerational wealth transfer from fund members

items.title: Shield, First Guardian collapse triggers MIS oversight consultation
items.teaser: On 23 September, Treasury launched its consultation paper on proposed improvements to regulatory visibility of the MIS sector through enhanced data collection after the Shield and First Guardian failures revealed “gaps in the regulators’ visibility of the sector” and highlighted the value of adequate, timely and…

items.title: Praemium chair departs early
items.teaser: Praemium has announced its chair Barry Lewin has departed the board after almost a decade. He first took on the non-executive chair role in May 2017 and had been scheduled to depart after the company’s annual general meeting on 14 October.

items.title: Antares Equities veteran resigns ahead of Janus Henderson takeover
items.teaser: Antares Equities' portfolio manager and head of fundamentals will conclude a long-serving tenure at the firm and will not transition to its soon-to-be parent company Janus Henderson.
items.ai_summary: • **John Guadagnuolo**, a 18-year veteran at Antares Equities, is resigning and will not move to Janus Henderson. • This change may impact the firm's investment team structure but does not affect its Fixed Income or Fairview Equity Partners businesses.

items.title: Netwealth to Acquire Paradino
items.teaser: Technology and super platform, Netwealth has announced it will acquire AI automation and productivity platform, Paradino.
items.ai_summary: • **Netwealth** is acquiring **Paradino**, an AI automation platform, to enhance adviser tools. • Advisers should prepare for new automation tools that may change how they deliver advice and manage client portfolios.

items.title: IGR predicts drawdowns will be major source of retirement income
items.teaser: The report states that drawing down accumulated superannuation will become an increasingly significant part of retirement income for many retirees and is estimated to increase from 2.5 per cent of GDP in 2025–26 to 5.8 per cent of GDP in 2065–66.
items.ai_summary: • **Drawdowns** from superannuation are expected to rise from 2.5% to 5.8% of GDP by 2065–66. • Advisers should prepare clients for retirement income strategies that rely more on superannuation pensions than the Age Pension.

items.title: CPA urges super funds to solve retirement phase or risk locking trillions out of the economy
items.teaser: Richard Webb, CPA Australia Superannuation Lead, said the new Retirement Standard from Association of Super Funds Australia comes amid concerns that many retirees are reluctant to draw on their super savings, despite Australia managing one of the world’s largest retirement asset pools.
items.ai_summary: • **Australia’s superannuation system manages $4.5 trillion**, but retirees struggle to convert savings into sustainable income. • **Super funds must improve retirement income strategies** to help members spend their savings comfortably and avoid locking trillions out of the economy.

items.title: Pacific AM to land SMA solutions Down Under, appoints investment chief
items.teaser: Pacific Portfolio Solutions, the related body corporate of Pacific Asset Management, will bring the latter's SMA solutions to Australia from the UK, welcoming an industry stalwart to chart the course.
items.ai_summary: • **Pacific AM will launch SMA solutions in Australia**, including Moderate, Balanced, Income, Growth, High Growth, and Listed Growth portfolios. • **Kyle Lidbury has been appointed as chief investment officer** to lead the investment team and oversee portfolio construction and adviser communications.

items.title: Praemium brings forward chair succession
items.teaser: Praemium will bring forward its leadership transition at board level, with its current chair stepping down as the platform and portfolio administration business continues to expand its focus on high-net-worth investors and technology.
items.ai_summary: • Praemium's chair, Barry Lewin, steps down effective 22 September 2026 **(date)** • Advisers should note the shift in focus to high-net-worth investors and technology **(focus area)**

items.title: Rest director for product departs
items.teaser: The general manager, product at Rest has left the super fund after nearly four years.
items.ai_summary: • Thin — open source

items.title: Advisers missing the third retirement risk, warns Aged Care Steps
items.teaser: Aged Care Steps is urging advisers to plan for frailty risk alongside longevity and sequencing risk, after its latest whitepaper found older Australians are spending more of their retirement with severe disability.
items.ai_summary: • Severe disability period for men aged 65 rose from 3.5 to 4.6 years **(increase)** • Advisers should consider frailty risk alongside longevity and sequencing risk **(advice focus)**

items.title: AGS acquires Hartley Financial in competitive market
items.teaser: AGS Financial Group, a Sydney financial planning and accounting firm, has completed the full acquisition of Hartley Financial. Hartley will bring two NSW and one Melbourne office to AGS Financial Group with the acquisition expected to add around $2.6 million in annual revenue.

items.title: Pinnacle affiliate appoints former Perpetual CIO
items.teaser: Former Perpetual chief investment officer, Kyle Lidbury, has departed to take on a new role at Pinnacle affiliate Pacific Portfolio Solutions (PPS).

items.title: Retirement confidence lags as investors turn to AI
items.teaser: Retirement has emerged as a central for investors globally, but a lack of confidence and financial literacy is keeping many savers on the sidelines, according to Amundi's latest global investor study.
items.ai_summary: • **23%** of investors are very confident about retirement, down from 26% last year; • Advisers can boost confidence by providing professional advice, as **half of advised investors** are very confident

items.title: UBS appoints ‘head of purpose’ in not-for-profit shake-up
items.teaser: UBS is renaming its not-for-profit segment to a ‘for purpose’ division as Anthony Hamawi is appointed from JBWere to head up the department. Hamawi will be joining UBS in mid-October as head of for purpose organisations, reporting to Wayne Gordon (head of advisory & sales, Australia).
items.ai_summary: • **UBS** is renaming its not-for-profit segment to ‘for purpose’; • **Anthony Hamawi** is joining UBS from JBWere to lead the new division

items.title: Vietnam joins FTSE Russell emerging market index
items.teaser: Vietnam has officially joined the FTSE Russell Global Equity Index Series, marking a new phase for its capital market as it moves from frontier to Secondary Emerging Market status.
items.ai_summary: • **Vietnam** joined the FTSE Russell Emerging Market Index on 21 September 2026; • Advisers should consider Vietnam as a new market opportunity with improved access for international investors

items.title: How Nvidia’s Jensen Huang could reshape geopolitics for investors
items.teaser: Stanford University professor Stephen Kotkin says computing power will become the key geopolitical contest between the US and China, predicting Nvidia founder and chief executive Jensen Huang will become an increasingly central figure in international relations.
items.ai_summary: • thin — open source

items.title: Privacy reforms well-meaning but mustn’t increase advice complexity: FAAA
items.teaser: Responding to the Government’s consultation of the Privacy Amendment (Personal Data Protection) Bill 2026, the FAAA has argued that further refinement is needed as the current proposal could add further data consent requirements for advisers without delivering any tangible consumer benefit.

items.title: The New Class of Adviser: Vertical integration and the case for advice practices
items.teaser: On 19 August, Financial Services Minister Dr Daniel Mulino announced, among other reforms, that the government would push ahead the ‘New Class of Adviser’ (NCA), but they would be limited to superannuation funds and insurance providers.
items.ai_summary: • thin — open source

items.title: FAAA flags gaps in discretionary trusts tax reforms, deficient framework
items.teaser: Under the proposed minimum tax on discretionary trust reforms, the Financial Advice Association Australia (FAAA) highlighted concerns over trustees potentially being forced to make "major and largely irreversible decisions" before the rules and guidance have been finalised.
items.ai_summary: • **FAAA highlights gaps in discretionary trusts tax reforms** with concerns over trustees making irreversible decisions before final rules are set; • **Advisers must stay informed on the proposed 30% minimum tax** and consider the new exemption options for discretionary trusts

items.title: What the 2026 Intergenerational Report means for advisers
items.teaser: Focus Partners Australia says this week’s Intergenerational Report highlights a world where Aussies will be living longer and retirement last longer.
items.ai_summary: • **Life expectancy in Australia is projected to reach 90 years for women and 86.1 years for men by 2066**; • **Retirement planning must adapt to longer lifespans** with increased healthcare and wealth transfer complexities

items.title: Esencia Wealth ads MDA licence through Generation Wealth merger
items.teaser: Esencia Wealth has added a managed discretionary account capability to its arsenal through a merger with Generation Wealth Partners, as it pushes ahead with its growth-by-merger strategy.

items.title: Beyond traditional bucketing: Why advisers are rethinking SMSF retirement strategies
items.teaser: Retirement bucketing strategies have long been a cornerstone of SMSF retirement planning, helping retirees manage sequencing risk by separating short-term spending needs from longer-term growth assets.
items.ai_summary: • **New research suggests guaranteed lifetime income is critical for retirement planning**; • **Combining bucketing with lifetime income solutions improves retirement outcomes** for SMSF members

items.title: The ‘kids’ inheriting older clients’ wealth might soon be retirees themselves
items.teaser: The conventional wisdom that the kids of advisers’ oldest clients stand to inherit their wealth might be overlooking the fact that by the time it happens these “kids” are likely to be near or in retirement themselves.
items.ai_summary: • **Treasury’s 2026 Intergenerational Report** shows inheriting clients’ wealth may soon go to retirees, not younger generations. • Advisers should consider targeting grandchildren for new clients as the traditional client succession model changes.

items.title: Confusion Driving Consumers Away From Life Insurance
items.teaser: Nearly half of Australian consumers considering life insurance feel confused and unconvinced by what they encounter, according to a new global report, with many abandoning the purchase before it is complete.
items.ai_summary: • **48% of Australians** feel confused about life insurance, leading to abandoned purchases. • **Confusion** is a key barrier to life insurance uptake, highlighting a need for clearer product communication.

items.title: ART-owned G'day Group invests $200m in regional holiday parks
items.teaser: Australian Retirement Trust (ART) owned G'day Group plans to invest more than $200 million in regional holiday parks in the lead up to the 2032 Olympic Games.
items.ai_summary: • **ART-owned G'day Group is investing $200m in regional holiday parks** in Queensland ahead of the 2032 Olympic Games. • Advisers should note the expansion of holiday parks and potential increased demand for accommodation in regional areas due to major events.

items.title: Questions raised about how ATO will deal with investment strategy documentation
items.teaser: In a Q&A session at the ASF Audit Technical Seminar last week, Burgess said if SMSF trustees are now going to have to provide the ATO with investment strategies, he questioned what it will be looking for in its reviews of them.
items.ai_summary: • **ATO may review SMSF investment strategies**, with concerns about what they will look for in terms of diversification. • Advisers should be aware that auditors already review these strategies annually, and the ATO's role in this area is unclear.

items.title: Fewer, clearer decisions: Hamilton Wealth takes the OCIO route
items.teaser: An idea that started with a conversation in New York has led to Hamilton Wealth Partners opt for an outsourced chief investment officer (OCIO) arrangement.
items.ai_summary: • **Hamilton Wealth is adopting an OCIO model** to streamline decision-making and reduce reliance on product-specific advice. • Advisers should consider the benefits of OCIO models in managing complexity and aligning with client needs.

items.title: Clients’ prolonged ‘frailty years’ is a risk advisers must consider
items.teaser: Data shows that older Australians are spending a larger share of retirement with severe disability.
items.ai_summary: • Frailty risk is rising, with men over 65 now spending 4.6 years with severe disability (up from 3.5 years) and women spending 6.4 years (up from 5.5 years)

items.title: Big data could help predict the next big advice ‘calamity’
items.teaser: FAAA chief executive officer Sarah Abood wants technology to be used to head off the next disaster in the financial advice space. Predictive models offer the opportunity to use data to detect and prevent the next collapse.
items.ai_summary: • Big data could help predict major advice scandals by analysing patterns like advisers managing thousands of clients

items.title: New education requirements linked to ATO’s existing courses
items.teaser: Peter Burgess, CEO of the SMSFA, told attendees at the ASF Audits Technical Seminar Treasury issued a document regarding SMSF trustee education shortly after the announcement in August from Financial Services Minister, Daniel Mulino.

items.title: How battles over super could rewrite long-term advice strategies
items.teaser: Australia’s superannuation framework has long been a recurring topic of debate across the political spectrum, touted as being the ‘envy of the world’, but it is also a large pool of funds – around $4.8 trillion at present – and many are looking at it as a saviour while people do it tough.
items.ai_summary: • **One Nation proposed allowing Australians to access 3% of their super contributions for up to three years to help with home ownership**. • Advisers must consider how policy changes like this could impact long-term advice strategies and client financial planning.

items.title: New NEOS Partnership
items.teaser: NEOS has announced a new integration with the AI automation platform Paradino, which it says gives financial advisers direct access to indicative pricing across all products on the NEOS Platform within their existing advice workflows.
items.ai_summary: • **NEOS has integrated with Paradino to give advisers direct access to indicative pricing across all products within their existing workflows**. • This integration supports advisers in providing informed advice by streamlining access to insurance insights.

items.title: Life Insurance Affordability – Poll
items.teaser: Our latest poll is taken from recently-released consumer research which suggests the life insurance affordability barrier is often a matter of perception rather than reality.
items.ai_summary: • thin — open source

items.title: Intergenerational Report looks to AI to buoy productivity slump
items.teaser: Australia's economy will continue to stagnate over the next 40 years, growing at just 2% annually, according to the latest Intergenerational Report (IGR), which points to the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution to buoy sagging productivity.
items.ai_summary: • Australia's economy is projected to grow at 2% annually over the next 40 years, below the 3% experienced previously • Advisers should consider AI's potential impact on productivity and economic growth when advising clients

items.title: Something’s wrong when the biggest bill lands with the smallest players
items.teaser: Advice networks are the least “valuable” links in the wealth management chain, yet when something goes wrong they’re too often left to carry the can, even when a failure is not their fault.
items.ai_summary: • **Advisers and licensees earned only $11 million** for a year’s work across $48.2 billion under advice. • **Platform and insurer profits are hidden from advisers’ accounts**, impacting their revenue and profitability, which advisers must understand when advising clients.

items.title: Definition of trust needs to be ‘crystal clear’ warns SMSFA
items.teaser: In its submission to Treasury on the exposure draft, the SMSFA said a significant concern for SMSFs and broader superannuation sector is the potential emergence of two separate and inconsistent tests for determining when trust income should receive concessional superannuation taxation treatment.
items.ai_summary: • **Trust income classification could become inconsistent** due to potential separate tests for concessional taxation; • **Advisers must ensure clarity in trust definitions** to avoid unintended tax outcomes
